title: Numbers 1-10 Practice Pages

unmappedSkills.description: Recognize and color/identify the written word for numbers 1-10 (one, two, three...)
Represent a given number by filling in circles on a ten frame

gaps: number-practice-page: single-number focus page with 4-5 activities on one sheet — tracing/writing, ten frame fill-in, number word coloring, object counting (color N stars). Repeatable template across numbers 1-10 (or 1-20).

components.name: Number Practice Page (one per number, 1-10)
components.description: Each page focuses on a single number and includes 4 activities: (1) Trace and write — large dotted number to trace plus a writing line with repeated practice, (2) Show on ten frame — empty 2x5 grid where student fills in the correct number of circles, (3) Color the number word — the word (e.g. 'one', 'two') printed in outline/bubble letters for coloring, (4) Color N stars — row of stars where student colors the correct quantity. Header: 'Numbers Practice' with Name/Date fields.
designPatterns: Single-number focus: one page per number prevents overwhelm. Deep practice on one concept.
Multi-activity page: 4 different activities for one number = 4 representations (digit, word, ten frame, quantity). Builds number sense from multiple angles.
Tracing as scaffolding: dotted numbers provide the motor path before independent writing.
Ten frame as representation tool: builds toward mental math fluency later.
Coloring as engagement: the number word coloring and star coloring are low-pressure activities that keep attention.
Consistent template: same layout for every number. Reduces cognitive load — kid knows what to do by page 3.
B&W, light ink, generous spacing: perfect for home printers and developing fine motor skills.

notes: Clean, no-frills number practice pages. The strength is the multi-representational approach: same number shown as digit (writing), word (coloring), quantity (stars), and structured model (ten frame). This is how number sense is built — not just rote writing. The consistent template across 1-10 means a child learns the format once and can work independently. Very young learner focused (Pre-K to K). This is the youngest-targeted drop so far.
